summary: The 2026 LLM landscape is dominated by a handful of frontier vendors — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and a strong cohort of open-weight challengers led by DeepSeek, Mistral, and Alibaba's Qwen. Real-world developer adoption is driven as much by enterprise aggregator reach (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx) as by direct API volume, which favors widely-distributed models. Because much of the live research data references unreleased or speculatively-named successor models, this ranking is deliberately limited to models that are confirmably publicly available and not deprecated today.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: Remains OpenAI's most broadly deployed multimodal workhorse, with massive API call volume and availability through Azure OpenAI Service, making it the default enterprise model across countless integrations.
models.best_for: General-purpose multimodal applications and production chat assistants

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's mid-tier Sonnet is the most-used coding model among developers and is available through AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and direct API, giving it very broad enterprise reach.
models.best_for: Software development, agentic workflows, and long-document analysis

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: Google's cost-efficient Flash model sees enormous token throughput via Vertex AI and consumer integrations, with high adoption for high-volume, low-cost workloads.
strengths: Native Vertex AI / Google Cloud integration
models.best_for: High-volume, latency-sensitive, and cost-sensitive production workloads

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Google's flagship reasoning model enjoys strong enterprise adoption through Vertex AI and Workspace, favored for complex reasoning and multimodal tasks across large context.
models.best_for: Complex reasoning, multimodal analysis, and large-context enterprise tasks

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: The leading open-weight model by download and adoption, DeepSeek V3 offers near-frontier performance at very low cost and is widely self-hosted and available across aggregators.
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive deployments and self-hosted open-weight applications

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek's open reasoning model remains hugely popular on HuggingFace for its transparent chain-of-thought reasoning at a fraction of proprietary reasoning model costs.
models.best_for: Reasoning-heavy and math/logic tasks on a budget

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: Meta's Llama 3.3 70B remains one of the most-downloaded open models on HuggingFace and is available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Vertex AI, anchoring countless fine-tuned derivatives.
strengths: Strong general performance for its size

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's fast, low-cost Haiku tier is widely adopted for high-throughput agentic and classification tasks and is available via Bedrock and Vertex AI.
models.best_for: High-volume agentic tasks, classification, and real-time assistants

models.name: o3
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's flagship reasoning model is heavily used for complex coding and STEM tasks via API and Azure, with growing adoption for agentic reasoning workflows.
models.best_for: Complex reasoning, advanced coding, and STEM problem-solving

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Mistral's flagship remains a popular European-sovereign choice, available via Azure, AWS Bedrock, and Vertex AI, favored by EU enterprises for data-residency reasons.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: Alibaba's flagship open-weight MoE model has rapidly climbed HuggingFace download charts and is widely adopted in Asia and among the open-weight community for its strong performance.
models.best_for: Open-weight multilingual deployments and cost-efficient self-hosting
